newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares close lower as blue chips fall.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares close lower as blue chips fall.

text.p: Philippine shares ended modestly lower for the fourth straight session on Friday bruised by selling on most blue chips, traders said.
"This is just a temporary slowdown after recent gains," said Mayenne Catimbang, research head at Magnum International.
"We are in a correction phase and this will go on until we hit the support level of 2,700," Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities said.
The main index closed 15.64 points lower at 2,762.80. Week-on-week, the main index shed 46.65 points from the previous Friday's level of 2,809.45.
Some of the main falls were in firstliners Meralco B Metrobank, PLDT and San Miguel Corp B. Meralco B dropped six percent to 140 pesos.

Empire East Land Holdings Inc toomk a battering to the surprise of most traders who believed that the issue had started to recover from fears of a property glut and financial woes. Empire ended at an all-time low close of 2.95 pesos. Briefly, in mid-trade the issue touched an all-time low of 2.85 pesos.
Traders said some investors who prefer to keep liquid may be selling ahead of the Empire's announcement of the ex-date for its 88 percent stock dividend.
Other mass-property issues, however, posted gains led by Filinvest Land Inc and C&P Homes after the Central Bank said it was relaxing rules on loans for low- and medium-cost homes.
In the broader market, decliners were doubled that of gainers at 73 to 35 with total turnover still weak at 1.8 billion pesos.
"For next week, the market will look at how the Dow will perform tonight after the release of a key U.S. monthly employement report," said Carl Valentin, analyst at Asia Pacific Capital.
Magnum's Catimbang said that the market will look at the Dow for direction as most of the macroeconomic domestic news have been released.
